speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing neck and arm pain, along with paresthesias and muscle weakness. To help me pinpoint the cause, could you tell me how long you have had these symptoms, and is the pain radiating down a specific arm or both sides?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient has a year-long history of burning neck and arm pain with paresthesias and recent bilateral hand weakness. Given his age, diabetes, and hypertension, do you have any numbness in your groin area or difficulty with bladder/bowel control? Also, have you noticed any issues with balance or coordination when walking?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy with C5-C6 radiculopathy.

The patient's history of a year-long burning pain, bilateral hand weakness, absent reflexes, and fasciculations is classic for cervical myelopathy, not a urinary tract infection. Given his diabetes and the progressive nature, I need to confirm the level and severity of compression. REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI
